summary: This diff adds real dependency-blocking enforcement to pms-issue-service.ts: updateIssue() now rejects a transition into a 'completed'-group status if any real pmsIssueRelations predecessor (via 'blocks' or 'blocked_by', in either direction) is not itself complete, and addIssueRelation() rejects creating a new blocking relation that would immediately leave an already-completed successor with an incomplete predecessor. I verified the direction semantics of the new predecessorIdsOf() helper against the existing normalizeEdges() in schedule-service.ts and they match exactly (both 'blocks' and 'blocked_by' rows resolve to the same predecessor/successor pairs), so the claimed consistency with the established convention is real, not asserted. All new queries are correctly orgId-scoped and run inside the existing withTenantContext() transaction; the pmsStatusGroupEnum 'completed' value and pmsIssueRelationTypeEnum values referenced in the new code both exist in schema.ts as used. The diff is purely additive (no schema/migration/auth/RLS changes), touches only the one service file plus its colocated test file and an ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml entry, and the claim entry correctly documents a collision check that I confirmed finds no other active claim on this file. The new test file only covers the pure predecessorIdsOf() function rather than the full service functions, but this matches this codebase's established pattern (confirmed via erp-fixed-assets-service.test.ts) of not exercising withTenantContext/a live DB from .test.ts files in the absence of a test-DB harness; I was unable to actually execute the test suite in this review sandbox since node_modules/drizzle-orm is not installed here, so this is a code-read verification, not a live test run. This is a low-blast-radius, well-scoped, correctly cross-checked change appropriate for tier1 autonomous merge.
issues: Read-check-write is not immune to a rare race: two concurrent requests inside separate transactions at Postgres's default READ COMMITTED isolation could both read pre-change state and both pass their respective checks, e.g. two relations added concurrently or a status update racing a relation add, before either write commits. Given this is human-driven PM usage rather than a high-concurrency hot path, this is a low-priority follow-up, not a blocker.

A predecessor issue that is 'cancelled' (rather than 'completed') will permanently block its successor from ever being marked complete, since only the 'completed' status group satisfies the check -- possibly an unintended product gap worth a follow-up decision (should a cancelled predecessor unblock its successor?), not a bug in the code as written.

addIssueRelation() does not guard against a self-referencing relation (issueId === relatedIssueId); this is a pre-existing gap in the function, not introduced by this diff, but sits directly adjacent to the new logic touched here.
